messages:
maria: Ran an nsys trace on the flash-fuse attention variant with KV prefetching turned on (opt-level=3). Seeing periodic 3-5ms spikes on kernel write paths that line up with high stall cycles. attaching a small excerpt from the timeline below.

maria: nsys command I used: `nsys profile --sample=none -o /tmp/trace.nsys --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --stats=true --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi` then perfetto view.

maria: perfetto snippet: ```
Kernel: flash_fuse_attn_prefetch
SMs: 72
Duration: 0.8ms avg, spikes to 4.6ms
Events: kv_write_async, l2_evict, shared_mem_stall
```

kai: hmm, are the spikes correlated with larger sequences or with specific batch sizes?

maria: spikes show up at batch sizes >= 16 and when seq_len > 1024. For small batches no problem. Also more frequent when we enable aggressive prefetch (prefetch_distance=4).

devon: Could be prefetch thrashing the L2 and forcing writebacks. Any evidence of cache line aliasing? nvprof /pc sampling might show.

maria: I grabbed a single-nsight sample. see this short log: ```
0.0012s kernel_start flash_fuse_attn_prefetch
0.0028s kv_cache_write (32KB)
0.0030s l2_eviction (lines: 128)
0.0054s kernel_end
```

lucas: If prefetch writes are landing in the same bank/way as the KV reads the SM could serialize. Also check shared mem bank conflicts — I've seen sharedmem->global writebacks stall kernels like this.

kai: quick theory: our kernel selection heuristic defaults to fused-flash when seq_len high, but maybe for these batch/seq combos fused+prefetch is worse than separate KV write + streaming attention. Worth toggling selection.

maria: did an A/B: forcing fallback to separate-attn + explicit kv_write kernel reduces spike 4.6ms -> 1.1ms median. CPU-side prefetch pacing also helps.

devon: good signal. Let's capture a perfetto with mem-copy track and HBM counters next. I can add a small test harness to sweep batch/seq/prefetch_distance.

maria: adding results to the shared bench in case someone wants to reproduce: `/bench/traces/1916012345-flash-prefetch-run1.pb`. tracebot: added tag `perf/regression` :thumbsup:

tracebot: Auto-note: Trace uploaded to perfdb. Link: https://perfdb.redwood/test/1916012345

lucas: Actionable: 1) adjust kernel selection to prefer non-prefetch fused or split path when batch>=16 && seq>=1024 2) add L2 eviction counters to our runtime telemetry 3) limit prefetch_distance by model size. Can create PR for selection rules.

maria: I'll open the RFC + perf logs. thanks all :tada:
